source.title: Tracking the Feature Dynamics in LLM Training: A Mechanistic Study
source.authors: Yangfan Xu; Yi Wang; Heng-Guan Huang; Hao Wang

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures SAE-feature semantics and decoder-direction changes during LLM training. Its results qualify the idea that SAE features are stable units, while also reporting SAE-extracted semantic features in LLMs.
record.gate_note: The study does not test toy-model superposition, feature sparsity or importance as causes of geometry, neuron polysemanticity, or whether features are distributed across neurons. Its own SAE-feature formation and drift measurements bear on the LLM/SAE portions of V4 and on V5. SAE training-speed comparisons and results cited from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAEs as an assumed tool to follow features across Pythia and Stanford GPT-2 training checkpoints. Its results are about training dynamics: how activations cluster around each feature's top-k datapoints, and how decoder directions drift towards their final values. It never tests whether features are superposed or spread across neurons, or whether an SAE recovers the model's features (V4). It does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units of a given model (V5). Direction drift and semantic shifts of fixed indices are measured across checkpoints of a model that keeps changing. They are partly shaped by recurrent SAE initialization, so they do not show that the dictionary units of a fixed model are non-canonical. These findings fit no version and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors introduce SAE-Track, which recurrently initializes SAEs across checkpoints. They conclude that features evolve in three phases (initialization/warmup, emergent, convergent) through maintaining, shifting and grouping patterns. Token-level features exist early and concept-level features form gradually. Decoder directions drift substantially, including after features are semantically formed, and fully stabilize only late in training.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains recurrently initialized SAEs on LLM activations across training checkpoints; it does not use the original toy-model superposition setup or measure the original superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports a model-specific early feature-collapse problem, most pronounced in stanford-gpt2-small-a. It says results are mainly consistent across tested model scales and layers, with an initialization-related UMAP difference for Stanford GPT-2. It also reports that changing similarity metrics does not substantially affect the overall conclusions.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE-identified token-level features show high datapoint clustering from initialization, while concept-level features form gradually in a low-rise-stable pattern during pretraining (Pythia-410M L4; consistent across other scales and layers).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In LLM pretraining, token-level SAE features exist from initialization and concept-level features emerge gradually.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE decoder directions drift substantially during training and keep moving after a feature's semantics stabilize, converging only late in training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The semantic stabilization of SAE features during training is decoupled from the stabilization of their directions.

fits_no_version.finding: Early-training activation collapse (near-1 cosine similarity) in stanford-gpt2-small-a disrupts similarity-based feature tracking.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Early activation collapse in some models undermines similarity-based feature analyses at those checkpoints.

record.problems: Feature semantic labels rely on manual inspection and are described as subjective. The main text provides qualitative trends but no numeric values or uncertainty estimates for the feature-formation and drift results. The analysis is limited to mid-scale models with available checkpoints; the paper also reports a model-specific early feature-collapse problem.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix figures for additional Pythia scales, Stanford GPT-2 medium, and Pythia-410M-deduped layers 8, 12, 16, and 20 show progress measures, cosine similarities, or trajectories, but the text gives no separate quantified outcomes for each condition beyond broad consistency statements. Their figure-only details were not added as separate rows. SAE training-speed and reconstruction comparisons in Appendix I were omitted because they evaluate the proposed SAE-Track method rather than the claim's representational properties.

untested.parts: All: toy models, sparsity-dependent transition, geometry.
All: capacity competition as the cause of polysemanticity.
Whether features are spread across neurons or recoverable by SAEs. SAE recovery is assumed rather than evaluated against any reference.
Completeness, and canonicity or stability across independently trained SAEs, sizes or methods on a fixed model. Divergence across SAE retraining is mentioned only as a cited result.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 and V5 labels are removed. Interpretable SAE features in Pythia are presupposed, not tested as evidence of superposition or recovery. Drift across training checkpoints is a different construct from V5's canonicity of units in a fixed model. The study cites Toy Models of Superposition but does not test it. The main-text results are qualitative, figure-based and without uncertainty; the semantic labels are manual.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, more features than dimensions, overlap and near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemantic neurons or important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.

The study analyzes SAE-extracted features, not whether features are distributed across many neurons. It does not establish SAE completeness or compare recovered features with a ground-truth feature set.

The study tests feature stability and semantic tracking across training checkpoints, but not whether SAE features are complete or canonical across SAE methods, datasets, or independently trained SAEs.
The paper analyzes individual decoder vectors but does not test whether the model's represented features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: Pythia-410M-deduped
rows.operation_detail: Measured the Feature Formation Progress Measure for token-level features in activation space across training checkpoints.
rows.measure: Within-set cosine similarity of top-k activating datapoints minus similarity for randomly sampled datapoints.
rows.baseline: Randomly sampled datapoints (subtracted in the progress measure).
rows.value: Token-level features typically exhibit high values from the start of training.
rows.note: The text describes the trend; no numeric values are stated.
rows.check: The progress measure is clustering of a feature's top-k datapoints relative to random datapoints across training. It does not measure distribution across neurons or SAE recovery of the model's features, so it does not bear on V4.

rows.subject: Pythia-410M-deduped
rows.operation_detail: Measured the Feature Formation Progress Measure for concept-level features in activation space across training checkpoints.
rows.measure: Within-set cosine similarity of top-k activating datapoints minus similarity for randomly sampled datapoints.
rows.baseline: Randomly sampled datapoints (subtracted in the progress measure).
rows.value: Concept-level features generally start lower and increase gradually throughout training.
rows.note: The text describes a gradual rise; no numeric values are stated.
rows.check: Concept-level features forming gradually is a training-dynamics result, not evidence on V4's superposition or recovery claim.

rows.subject: Pythia-410M-deduped
rows.operation_detail: Measured the feature-space progress measure for token-level features across training checkpoints.
rows.measure: Within-set similarity of SAE-encoded feature vectors for top-k activating datapoints minus similarity for randomly sampled datapoints.
rows.baseline: Randomly sampled datapoints (subtracted in the progress measure).
rows.value: Token-level features typically exhibit high values from the start of training.
rows.note: The text describes the trend; no numeric values are stated.
rows.check: Same as R1, measured in SAE feature space; not a V4 measure.

rows.subject: Pythia-410M-deduped
rows.operation_detail: Measured the feature-space progress measure for concept-level features across training checkpoints.
rows.measure: Within-set similarity of SAE-encoded feature vectors for top-k activating datapoints minus similarity for randomly sampled datapoints.
rows.baseline: Randomly sampled datapoints (subtracted in the progress measure).
rows.value: Concept-level features generally start lower and increase gradually throughout training; their plateau is often more pronounced in feature-space plots.
rows.note: The text describes the trend; no numeric values are stated.
rows.check: Same as R2, measured in feature space; not a V4 measure.

rows.subject: Pythia-410M-deduped
rows.operation_detail: Compared normalized decoder vectors at intermediate checkpoints with their respective final-checkpoint directions.

conditions.value: intermediate checkpoint direction versus final direction

rows.measure: Cosine similarity between decoder vectors and their final directions.
rows.value: Most feature directions undergo significant drift; cosine-similarity distributions start broad and skewed toward lower values, then shift toward 1 as training progresses.
rows.note: The text describes the distribution and trend but gives no numeric values; alignment eventually becomes high.
rows.check: Drift of decoder directions across checkpoints of a changing model does not test whether SAE features are canonical or stable units of a given model's representation (V5). Alignment rises to high values late in training.

rows.subject: Pythia-410M-deduped
rows.operation_detail: Tracked decoder-vector trajectories for features deemed semantically formed.
rows.measure: Directional movement of decoder vectors after the feature's semantic meaning is considered stable.
rows.baseline: Semantic stabilization of the same feature.
rows.value: Formed-feature trajectory segments still exhibit noticeable movement; individual directions continue to change after semantic meaning stabilizes.
rows.note: The text explicitly distinguishes semantic stabilization from directional stabilization; no numeric movement values are stated.
rows.check: Directions keep moving after semantic stabilization during training. This is a training-dynamics result, not a test of V5 stability for a fixed model.

rows.subject: Pythia-410M-deduped
rows.operation_detail: Tracked fixed SAE feature indices by inspecting changes in their top-k activating examples across checkpoints.

conditions.value: 256 random sampled features for transition statistics

rows.measure: Semantic change patterns inferred from top-k activating examples.
rows.baseline: Earlier-checkpoint examples for the same tracked feature index.
rows.value: The paper reports maintaining, shifting, and grouping patterns; some features change semantic association or organize from diffuse activations into coherent features.
rows.note: The paper also notes that semantic labeling relies on manual inspection and is subjective.
rows.check: Semantic shifting or grouping of a fixed SAE index across checkpoints reflects model training and the recurrent-initialization tracking scheme. The paper calls the method a study tool, not a consistency test. The labels come from subjective manual inspection, and the 256-feature statistics appear only in a figure.

rows.subject: stanford-gpt2-small-a
rows.operation_detail: Measured activation similarity and SAE feature-formation tracking at early checkpoints; the paper identifies a feature-collapse case.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity among activations or features and resulting disruption to feature tracking.
rows.value: Activations or features converge to near-1 cosine similarity; the resulting measure is suppressed near zero and tracking can show disruptions or phase shifts. Severe collapse is reported for only one tested LLM, most pronounced in this model.
rows.locator: Appendix K.2, Figures 23–26; Appendix L, Figure 43 and Sections L.1–L.2
rows.note: The paper attributes the tracking glitch to collapse and says it is model-specific; it reports that subsequent tracking remains usable after the collapse.
rows.check: Early 'feature collapse' is a near-1 cosine similarity among random activations that breaks the tracking metric. It is a measurement artifact in one model and bears on no version. The baseline is effectively the random-datapoint similarity, not 'not stated'.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
